childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Declaration
Augusta Sailing Club Proclamation
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription: The Augusta Sailing Club, one of the premier sailing organizations in the southeastern United States, has been holding the Halloween Regatta since their founding on July 24th, 1953. The Columbia County Board of Commissioners wishes to recognize the Augusta Sailing Club and congratulate them on the upcoming 72nd Halloween Regatta, which will  take place from October 9th – 11th, 2026.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Community and Emergency Services Committee
Chairman's Reappointment to the Columbia Judicial Circuit Public Defender Supervisory Panel
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:
The Columbia Judicial Circuit Public Defender Supervisory Panel is made up of three appointments, one by the Governor, one by the Chief Judge of the Columbia Circuit and one by the Chairman of the Columbia County Board of Commissioners. The Chairman would like to reappoint Keith Johnson to the Columbia Judicial Circuit Public Defender Supervisory Panel for a term ending June 30, 2031. 
A letter will be sent to the Georgia Public Defender Council upon approval of this request.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: New Accountability Court Clinical Case Manager Position
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:
Superior Court is requesting to add a new position of Accountability Court Clinical Case Manager. It is a grant funded, full-time Grade 22 position with entry salary of $21.49/hr. Superior Court already funds a Coordinator and Case Manager out of this same grant. They are simply adding this third position.

This position is funded by a grant awarded by the Council of Accountability Courts Judges State of Georgia program. The purpose of the Accountability Court Grants program is to make grants to local courts and judicial circuits to establish specialty courts or dockets to address offenders arrested for drug charges or mental health issues. This grant program is subject to the administrative rules established by the Criminal Justice Coordinating Council. The Subgrant period is from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027. This position will end when the grant funding ends.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Change Order #1 to Contract#2025-3123 with Goodwyn Mills Cawood for the Design of the Euchee Creek Greenway All Remaining Phases Project
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:
Location – This project is to construct various sections of 10-ft wide shared-use path to complete several connections of the Euchee Creek Greenway trail system programmed in TIA2. The sections include: 
  • Along William Few Pkwy from the trailhead near Baker Place Landfill to the existing Patriots Park Trail near the intersection of William Few Pkwy and Columbia Road.
  • Along William Few Pkwy from the existing Patriots Park Trail on the north side of the property to the future Riverwood Park near the intersection of Hardy McManus Rd and William Few Pkwy.
  • Along the GA Power Easement from Blanchard Woods Park to the future Riverwood Park near the intersection of Hardy McManus Rd and William Few Parkway.
 
Request – Approve Change Order #1 to Contract#2025-3123 with Goodwyn Mills Cawood for the Design of the Euchee Creek Greenway All Remaining Phases Project in the amount of $106,047.50.
 
History – On 3/4/25, the Board of Commissioners approved a contract with GMC in the amount of $417,760 for the Design of the Euchee Creek Greenway All Remaining Phases Project. GMC has completed preliminary engineering, are working towards final construction plans, and have identified the following scope and fee adjustments needed to deliver the project: 
  • -$25,050.00 from the original contract for structural design will not be needed
  • -$19,950.00 from the original contract for pedestrian crossing studies will not be needed
  • +$113,297.50 not included in the original contract for right-of-way services will be needed
  • +$37,750.00 additional for floodplain studies will be needed

Funding – TIA 2

Timeline – The consultant expects to have the right-of-way and floodplain submittals delivered within three (3) months of the issuance of the Notice-to-Proceed.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Bid# 2026027-BID2710 and Contract #2026-3708 with Peek Pavement Marking, LLC for the 2026 SAP Striping and Signs Project
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:
Location – Various County Roads (reference history below)
 
Request – Approve Bid# 2026027-BID2710 and Contract# 2026-3708 with Peek Pavement Marking, LLC for the 2026 SAP Striping and Signs Project in the amount of $378,736.34.
 
History –  On 7/21/26, the Board of Commissioners approved the acceptance of the 2026 LMIG Safety Action Plan Grant. Staff advertised the project and bids were opened on August 20, 2026, with the lowest, most responsive bidder being Peek Pavement Marking, LLC. The project includes striping, raised pavement markers (RPM), and sign replacement installation:
  • Louisville Rd, Old Washington Rd, and Dozier Rd to receive new striping, stop bars, RPMs, and signs.
  • William Few Pkwy, Ray Owens Rd, and Harlem Grovetown Rd to receive new RPMs only. 

Traffic Engineering and Operations will allocate the remaining $142,104.66 of the $520,841.00 grant toward upgrading rectangular rapid flashing beacons (RRFBs) in accordance with the grant application and acceptance of funds by the Board. Over the next six (6) months, staff will order and upgrade systems individually as time allows on the following corridors: William Few Pkwy, Blue Ridge Dr, Riverwood Pkwy, William Smith Blvd, Cox Rd, Flowing Wells Rd, and Ronald Reagan Dr.

Funding – 2026 SAP Grant
 
Timeline – The contractor will have 45-calendar days to complete the work from the issuance of the Notice-to-Proceed.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Change Order #1 to Contract #2025-3375 with UES Professional Solutions 18, LLC for Geotechnical Services on the Wrightsboro Rd Widening Project
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:
Location - Wrightsboro Rd from Jimmie Dyess Pkwy to Horizon South Pkwy

Request - Approve Change Order #1 to Contract# 2025-3375 with UES Professional Solutions 18, LLC for Geotechnical Services on the Wrightsboro Rd Widening Project in the amount of $373,765.89.

History - In May 2025, the Board of Commissioners entered into contract with Alfred Benesch & Company (Benesch) to deliver the Preliminary Engineering (PE) phase of the Wrightsboro Rd Widening
Project. Since the commencement of design, it was been determined that Geotechnical Services related to a Pavement Evaluation and a Limited Phase I Environmental Site Assement are required; however, these
services are outside Benesch's contracted scope of work. 

In December of 2025, the Board of Commissioners entered into contract with UES Professional Solutions 18, LLC to complete the required Pavement Evaluation and Limited Phase 1 Environmental Site Assessment in the amount of $49,048.13. This work has now been completed and the scope for the soil survey has been identified. This Change Order is to complete the required geotechnical work in accordance with GDOT and FHWA requirements. 

Funding - MPO/TIA Discretionary ​(80% Federal / 20% Local)

Timeline - This work will be done in coordination with the design contract with Benesch and is not expected to add any additional time to the project.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Resolution 26-20 Concerning a Determination to Abandon and Sell a Portion of Crawford Place Lane Labeled Tract 1
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:

Request - Approve Resolution 26-20 to abandon and sell a portion of Crawford Place Lane.

At the following Commissioners' Meeting, a report of the public hearing will be presented with a second Resolution proposing to abandon the ROW and proceed to a sale according to the Georgia State Law.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Purchase from Environmental Products Group an Envirosight RovverX Pipeline Inspection Camera for the Stormwater Operations Department
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:
Location - N/A

Request - Purchase of an Envirosight RovverX Pipeline Inspection Camera for the Stormwater Operations Department in the amount of $129,700.00.

History - The Stormwater Operations Department conducts inspections of newly installed underground storm sewer systems prior to the County accepting ownership, as well as inspections of 20% of the county's existing storm sewers every year as required by our MS4 Permit. The current camera (RapidView IBAK Inspection System) is over 10 years old, frequently malfunctions and needs repairs, and replacement parts are very limited. This downtime greatly reduces the inspection crew's production and efficiency. 

The purchase of the subject camera is to equip the inspection crew with more reliable equipment capable of meeting the constant inspection demand.   

Funding - Stomrwater Utility Fee - $129,700.00 (Sourcewell Purchase Contract Price)

Timeline - If approved, the department will order the camera and expects it to be delivered within 30-days.

childItems.agendaObjectItemName: Change Order #1 to Contract # 2026-3567 with East Coast Grading, Inc. for LMIG 2026
childItems.agendaObjectItemDescription:
Location - McCrary Ct. and Claudia Dr.

Request - Approve Change Order # 1 to Contract # 2026-3567 with East Coast Grading, Inc. for LMIG 2026 for an amount not to exceed $310,000.00.

History - Through the LMIG and LRA Programs the County has been granted $11,022,758.34, including a 10% match from the County.  As a condition of receiving the grants, all authorized funds must be spent in totality.  Currently the County has a shortfall of obligated expenditures, detailed as follows:
  • Total Funds Authorized through the LMIG and LRA Programs:                   $11,022,758.34
  • Total Funds Obligated through Contracts and Change Orders To Date:     $10,687,424.58
  • Balance of Unobligated Funds that must be spent:                                          $335,333.76

East Coast Grading, Inc. is currently under contract to complete work submitted for the LMIG 2026 program.  County staff has identified two roads in close proximity to the work being completed by East Coast Grading, McCrary Ct. and Claudia Dr., that are in need of rehabilitation. Staff contacted East Coast Grading to see if they were agreeable to holding the contract unit pricing for these roads.  An estimated price for McCrary Ct. was given in the amount of $101,395.20 and Claudia Dr. in the amount of $199,310.00 for a total of $300,705.20.  Staff requests approval of a change order not to exceed $310,000.00 in the event of unforeseen overages.

The remaining balance of unobligated funds are intended to cover some anticipated overages as a part of the LRA 2024 Contract with E.R. Snell.

Funding - LMIG

Timeline - N/A
